Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Drawings 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 

This standard establishes rules for modification in the drawings. Due to the day-to-day upgradation in the technolog}', 
changes either in manufacturing process or in component material are inevitable. It is therefore, important that 
drawings must record all these alterations or revisions. To have uniformity in the presentation of revisions, this 
standard defines the convenient methods of recording. 

This standard is expected to provide the broad guidelines to the persons working in the drawing and design offices, to 
facilitate the indications of revisions in drawings. 

It would also help in company standardization especially in regard to System CertificaUon documentation (ISO 9000) 
in connection with revision of technical drawings.

will be reviewed for harmonization with the International Standard. 



IS 14412 : 1996 



Indian Standard 



TECHNICAL DRAWINGS — INDICATION FOR 
REVISION OF DRAWINGS 



1 SCOPE 

This standard covers the methods for recording the 
aherations or revisions, which are made from time to 
time, in the drawings. 

2 REFERENCES 

The follovving standards contains provisions which 
through reference in this text, constitute provision of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below: 



IS No. 



Title 



8930 Technical product documentation 

(Part I) : 1995 vocabulary: Part 1 Terms relating 
to technical drawings — General and 
t>'pes of drawings ( first revision ) 

9609 Lettering on technical drawings: 

(Part 1) : 1983 Part I English lettering ( first 
revision ) 

10714 ; 1983 General principles of presentation on 

technical drawings 

11665 : 1985 Technical drawings— Title block 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions of 
drawings shall inckide all types of drawings mentioned 
in IS 8930 (Parti): 1995. * 

4 METHOD OF INDICATING CHANGE 

4.1 A convenient method of recording revisions is a 
table (revision panel) giving the revision number or let- 
ter, date, brief record and dated initials of the drawn and 
approving authority. The revision panel may be: 

a) a part of the title block ( see IS 1 1665 : 1985 and 
Fig- 1). 

b) at the top right hand corner (see Fig. 2). 

c) a separate document in continuation of the main 
drawing disseminating tlie revision infom^ations. 



5 REVISION NUMBER 

Every change in the drawing shall be assigned with a 
revision number, letter or identification mark. 

5.1 Each organization may adopt its own method of 
assigning revision number or letter and marking. Care 
should be taken to see that the record of revision is tied 
up into the drawing in such a manner that it may be 
easily found. 

5.1.1 All changes shall be carried out preferably by 
putting an identification mark, so that the original 
version is also available in the drawing for information. 

5.1.2 As and when a drawing is completly revised, 
then the revised drawing should also indicate the 
reference of the orginal drawing. 

6 LAYOUT OF REVISION PANEL 

6.1 It is recommended that the revision panel may be 
arranged in columns and rows {see Fig. 1 ) by means of 
continuously thick or thin lines. Type A or B of 
IS 10714 : 1983, to allow information to be entered under 
the following headings: 

a) Reference number, 

b) Briefrecord, 

c) Drawn, and 

d) Approving authority. 

NOTE — If necessary, more columns can be added to 
cover specific requirements. 

6.1.1 The reference numt)er' colunm shows the relevant 
revision number/letter or identification mark as shown 
on the drawing. 

6.1.2 The brief record' column shows the brief record 
of changes on the drawing. 

6.1.3 The drawn' column shows the dated initials of 
the person who carried out the changes in the drawing. 

6.1.4 The approving authority' column shows the 
dated initials of the approving authority. 

6.1.5 The revision panel can also contain other 
informations necessary for clarity regarding changes/ 
revision in the drawing.

7 ENTRIES 



7.1 Entries should be made in the relevant columns in 
horizontal rows. For clarity, it is recommended that each 
change of entry be separated by means of continuous 
thick or thin lines, TypeAorBofIS 10714: 1983. 

7.2 To facilitate extension of revision panel, entries for 
revision should begin from bottom upwards if the 
revision panel is a part of the title block (see Fig. 1) and 
from top downwards when revision panel is at the top 
right hand corner on drawing (see Fig.2). It is 
recommended that the word ditto or its equivalent 
abbreviations should not be used on drawings. 



7.3 The entries may be executed by means of free-hand 
lettering, stencilling, or any other appropriate means, 
preferably using capital letters as specified in IS 9609 



(rani ): iv5:>. 



8 SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS 



8.1 In conjunction with revisions to drawings, it is 
usual to issue a form or note to record the change, to 
ensure the replacement or correction of existing prints, 
and to give special instructions concerning disposition 
of any existing parts or work in progress. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1 986 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue 
of *BIS Handbook' and 'Standards : Monthly Additions'. 

This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc : No. LM 02 ( 41 14 ).
